title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the opening page of a section titled 'Foncteurs fibres motiviques et groupes fondamentaux motiviques' (previous page). X is a connected (pre)scheme. Motives over X form a Tannakian-type category with a motivic Galois (fundamental) group G, or a pro-system of finite-type quotients G_alpha. The T_alpha are the 'torseurs fondamentaux': torsors, or more accurately gerbes/groupoids, of fibre functors under G_alpha.

1) Case X_red of characteristic p>0. In general the T_alpha have no sections over Q. In modern terms, the motivic Tannakian category in characteristic p has no Q-valued fibre functor (Serre's supersingular elliptic curve / quaternion obstruction). Canonically one has only the following realizations.

(i) ell-adic points xi_ell^(alpha) in T_alpha(Z_ell) for ell != p, i.e. integral etale realizations. Grothendieck conjectures 'heuristically' that they all come from a single point over a product ring prod_{ell != p} Z_ell (written Z-tilde). This is an adelic, independence-of-ell type compatibility.

(ii) If k is a perfect field over X, a p-adic point xi_p^(alpha) in T_alpha(W(k)), the integral crystalline realization. Again it presumably comes from a point over a p-completed ring.

(iii) Its reduction xi_p^(alpha)0 in T_alpha(k), the mod-p Hodge-de Rham realization. The arrow labelled 'De Rham-Hodge' goes from the W(k)-point to the k-point.

Marginal programme:
- ell-adic cohomology.
- p-adic cohomology carries extra structure: semilinear ('1/2-linear') operators F and V (Frobenius, Verschiebung).
- Hodge-de Rham cohomology. One should probably work in the derived category, take the Witt/Hodge-de Rham structure into account, and relate it to the Hodge filtration (?).
- 'It should essentially be [Dieudonne-]Manin', i.e. the Dieudonne-Manin theory of F-crystals/isocrystals.

For X = Spec F_q there are in general non-trivial obstructions living in H^1(Q,G).

Normalization and uniqueness. Use fibre functors that induce the canonical functor on effective weight-0 motives (Artin motives / finite etale covers). This rigidifies the Galois/Artin part, so the relevant group becomes connected. Then:
- The Z_ell-points are probably unique up to isomorphism by Lang's theorem (Hensel plus Lang over the residue field F_ell for a smooth group with connected fibres).
- The same holds for W(k)-points when k is finite.
- More generally it should hold for k perfect of cohomological dimension 1 (?). This is exactly Steinberg's 1965 theorem (Serre's Conjecture I).
- Over a general k, T_alpha(k) may contain several isomorphism classes. Yet the limit T_infinity(k) = lim T_alpha(k) may have only one, namely the one given by Hodge-de Rham theory.

Purpose: to describe what replaces the missing Q-fibre functor in characteristic p (a family of integral ell-adic, crystalline and mod-p de Rham points of the motivic gerbe) and to show these are canonical up to isomorphism.
errors: Lang's theorem by itself gives triviality of torsors over finite fields. Over Z_ell one needs a smooth affine group scheme with connected fibres plus Hensel, i.e. an integral model of G_alpha with good properties, which is not established. Over Q_ell the analogous uniqueness can fail, since H^1(Q_ell, torus) can be non-zero; this is presumably why Grothendieck works integrally.

Passing to pro-groups needs care. Uniqueness for each alpha does not automatically give a point or uniqueness in the limit (lim^1 issues), although compactness helps over finite fields. Grothendieck's suggestion that T_infinity(k) is unique while the T_alpha(k) are not is heuristic.

The crystalline realization is semilinear-structured (F-crystals). Treating it as a W(k)-valued fibre functor ignores Frobenius, and the integral (torsion) behaviour of crystalline/de Rham cohomology is not exact. The margin itself notes that one must probably work in the derived category.
The cd<=1 extension is flagged '(?)'. It is true (Steinberg 1965) for connected linear groups over perfect fields of cd<=1, but connectedness after the weight-0 normalization is assumed, not proved.

ideas.what: In characteristic p the motivic gerbe has no Q-points; only ell-adic, crystalline and mod-p points exist
ideas.modern_name: Non-neutrality of the Tannakian category of motives over F_q; motivic gerbe with ell-adic and crystalline fibre functors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (no Q-, R-, Q_p-valued fibre functor), Saavedra Rivano 1972, Deligne-Milne 1982, Milne 1994, Langlands-Rapoport 1987
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's ideas reached print via Saavedra's thesis and Demazure/Kleiman; this specific page is unpublished

ideas.what: Integral fibre functors with values in Z_ell, W(k) and k (mod-p Hodge-de Rham), with the de Rham point as reduction of the crystalline point
ideas.modern_name: Integral realizations of motives; integral p-adic Hodge theory / crystalline-de Rham comparison mod p
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot, Mazur-Ogus, Fontaine-Messing, Bhatt-Morrow-Scholze (integral comparison); integral motivic Galois groups much less developed
ideas.where_published: Crystalline cohomology was announced in Grothendieck's 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposes, 1968). The Tannakian integral use appears unpublished.

ideas.what: Heuristic that all ell-adic points come from one point over a product ring (prod_{ell != p} Z_ell, or a completion of Z)
ideas.modern_name: Adelic / compatible-system realization; independence of ell
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (compatible systems), Deligne; Langlands-Rapoport adelic description

ideas.what: Normalize fibre functors on weight-0 (Artin) motives, then deduce uniqueness up to isomorphism of the Z_ell- and W(F_q)-valued fibre functors via Lang's theorem, and over perfect fields of cd<=1
ideas.modern_name: Triviality of torsors under connected reductive group schemes over henselian rings with finite / cd<=1 residue field (Lang, Steinberg); uniqueness of local fibre functors of the motivic gerbe
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lang 1956, Steinberg 1965; the uniqueness statements for motives over F_q in Langlands-Rapoport 1987 and Milne 1992/1994

ideas.what: Crystalline realization carries semilinear F, V; link with Hodge filtration; 'essentially Dieudonne-Manin'
ideas.modern_name: F-crystals, Dieudonne-Manin classification, Mazur's Newton-above-Hodge theorem
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux' (ICM 1970; Montreal 1974 lectures)

ideas.what: Conjecture: although T_alpha(k) may have several isomorphism classes, the pro-limit T_infinity(k) has a unique class, given by Hodge-de Rham
ideas.modern_name: No standard name; uniqueness of the mod-p de Rham fibre functor on the full motivic category

missed.claim: Over a general perfect field k, the mod-p fibre functors on finite-type quotients may be non-unique. On the full pro-motivic group, the k-valued fibre functor is conjectured unique up to isomorphism and equal to the Hodge-de Rham one.
missed.quote: il est possible que T_∞(k) = lim T_α(k) n'en ait qu'un à isom. près, celui donné par la théorie de De Rham Hodge
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and mod-p motivic Galois groups and their torsors are now approachable via prismatic cohomology and integral p-adic Hodge theory. A uniqueness statement for the de Rham/mod-p realization as a point of the integral motivic gerbe seems not to have been formulated or tested.

missed.claim: Uniqueness of local fibre functors on motives over finite fields is derived from Lang's theorem, and extended to perfect fields of cd<=1, i.e. Steinberg's theorem, the same year. This is done integrally (Z_ell, W(k)) after rigidifying the weight-0 part.
missed.quote: les déployés de T_α(Z_ℓ) sont sans doute uniques à isom. près (th. de Lang), de même aussi des T_α(W_p(k)) si k fini (id.), plus généralement pour un k parfait de dim coh 1 (?)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates the uniqueness of the ell-adic and crystalline 'local morphisms' of the pseudomotivic gerbe in Langlands-Rapoport/Milne. It does so via an integral, Lang-type argument rather than the rational Galois-cohomology computations used later.

missed.claim: All ell-adic integral points should come from a single point over a product of the Z_ell (and similarly at p): an integral adelic point of the motivic gerbe.
missed.quote: provenant sans doute de ξ_ℓ ∈ T_α(Z̃_{ℓZ}) ... heuristique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an integral form of independence of ell. Integral compatibility across all primes is still largely open.

deep.surprise_reason: Many ingredients later became standard (non-neutral motivic gerbe in characteristic p, ell-adic and crystalline fibre functors, Dieudonne-Manin). Notable unpublished details: the integral viewpoint (fibre functors over Z_ell, W(k), k), the Lang/Steinberg uniqueness argument after weight-0 normalization, and the specific conjecture that the pro-limit mod-p fibre functor is unique and equals Hodge-de Rham. All of this is sketched with question marks.
transcription_corrections: 'produits tensoriels fondamentaux' should almost certainly read 'torseurs fondamentaux (T_α)'.
'héréditaire [?]' (twice, right margin) is likely 'heuristique'; the second occurrence may be 'heuristique gratuit'.
Margin '1/2 linéaires' is Grothendieck's notation for 'semi-linéaires' (F and V semilinear).
'Si X = Spec F_q, il y a cas général des [?] structures non triviales' is more plausibly 'il y a en général des obstructions non triviales dans des H^1(Q,G)'.
'T_p(Z̃_{pZ})' in (ii) is likely T_α over a p-adic completion; the subscript is T_α, not T_p.
'(ii) ... si k est un corps parfait sur X' : the insertion reads 'k corps parfait sur X', replacing the struck 'X def. f. sur le corps parfait k'.
Margin 'Il doit s'agir essentiellement de ... Manin' probably refers to Dieudonné–Manin theory.
